note: MATERIAL DIVERGENCE, flagged not resolved: FAOSTAT 2022 shows just 9.2% -- well below both the project's derived (29%) and headline/official (46%) figures. Possible drivers: FAOSTAT's international commodity classification for 'Vegetables, Other' may be narrower than Statistikaamet's PM33 category; international reporting for minor-crop production in small countries can lag or under-count relative to the national statistics office's own figures; 2022 may also have been a weaker vegetable-production year than the years underlying the official 5-year average. This is the same vegetables/fruit gap already flagged as the project's largest unexplained divergence since Phase 1 -- FAOSTAT adds a THIRD data point that disagrees with both existing ones, rather than resolving the discrepancy. Treated as an open, documented uncertainty.

project_figure_source: self_sufficiency_model.csv note: raw rapeseed basis for the oil yield-cancellation proxy (PM37 2024)
note: MATERIAL DIVERGENCE, flagged not resolved: FAOSTAT 2022 raw-rapeseed self-sufficiency is 141.3%, roughly double the PM37-2024-derived figure (69.3%) this project's oil estimate is built on. Two plausible, unconfirmed drivers: (1) 2022 was an unusual year for Baltic/Black Sea region oilseed trade following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, which reshaped regional grain/oilseed flows -- a temporal effect, not necessarily a definitional one; (2) FAOSTAT's SUA/FBS accounting may treat seed crushed domestically for oil extraction differently from Statistikaamet's PM37 'domestic use' figure, particularly where the resulting oil is later exported. Not resolved -- presented as an open uncertainty.

project_figure_source: self_sufficiency_model.csv: Oils/fats/spreads (rapeseed) -- oil self-sufficiency via yield-cancellation from raw seed
note: CONFIRMS A FLAGGED LIMITATION: FAOSTAT 2022 refined-oil self-sufficiency is 265%, far above the 69.3% yield-cancellation proxy. Phase 5's own methodology note already flagged that the yield-cancellation argument 'breaks down if a meaningful share of Estonia's edible oil trade is in already-refined form rather than raw seed' -- this is exactly what FAOSTAT shows: Estonia produces far more refined rapeseed oil (61kt) than it consumes domestically (23kt supply), meaning a large share of crushed oil is exported directly as oil, not as raw seed. The true oil self-sufficiency is very likely well above the 69.3% raw-seed proxy, in Estonia's favour (i.e. the project's existing oils figure UNDERSTATES self-sufficiency, not overstates it) -- but the exact magnitude remains uncertain given the raw-seed-level divergence noted above.
